visa_routes.name: H-1B Specialty Occupation (cap-subject)

salary_threshold.note: No fixed national minimum; employer must pay at least the DOL prevailing/actual wage via an LCA. Since FY2027 the cap lottery is wage-weighted: higher OEWS wage level = more lottery entries (reported Level IV 4x, III 3x, II 2x, I 1x).

visa_routes.degree_requirement: Specialty occupation requiring a US bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in a specific related field (or equivalent via education + experience).
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: A 3-year Indian bachelor's is usually NOT accepted alone as a US bachelor's equivalent. WES may grant US-bachelor's equivalency only if earned in Division I from a NAAC 'A' or better institution; otherwise treated as 3 years of undergraduate study. For H-1B, USCIS regulations allow '3-for-1': three years of progressively responsible specialized experience may substitute for each missing year of college (8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(D)(5)), so a 3-year degree + 3 years relevant experience is commonly evaluated as a US bachelor's equivalent by a credential evaluator. The 3-for-1 substitution generally does not carry over to EB-2 green-card filings that require a single-source degree.
visa_routes.processing_time: Registration in March (FY2027 window 2026-03-04 to 2026-03-19); selections announced 2026-03-31; petitions filed from 1 April; employment start 1 October at earliest. Premium processing available for petitions.
visa_routes.lottery_or_quota: Annual cap 65,000 + 20,000 US-master's cap. FY2027 used the new wage-weighted selection (DHS final rule published 2025-12-29, effective 2026-02-27). Cap reached for FY2027; no second lottery. Cap-exempt employers (universities, affiliated nonprofits, research orgs) are not subject to the lottery.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Dual intent; employer can sponsor EB-2/EB-3 green card (PERM). Indian-born applicants face very long EB-2/EB-3 per-country backlogs (many years; check State Dept Visa Bulletin).
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: Employer pays registration, petition and legal fees. Proclamation 10973 (2025-09-19) added a $100,000 payment for certain NEW petitions for workers outside the US / requiring consular notification; extended 2026-09-18 to 2027-09-21, but the implementing policy was vacated by D. Mass. on 2026-06-08 and reported not being collected as of late Sept 2026. Change-of-status/extension petitions inside the US were exempt. A 2026-09-18 Executive Order adds closer review of employers with recent layoffs.

visa_routes.name: L-1A / L-1B Intracompany Transferee
visa_routes.degree_requirement: No degree requirement; worker must have been employed abroad by a qualifying related entity (parent/subsidiary/affiliate/branch) for 1 continuous year in the prior 3 years, as manager/executive (L-1A) or with specialized knowledge (L-1B).
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Degree not required, so a 3-year degree is not a barrier.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: L-1A managers may qualify for EB-1C (no PERM); still subject to India per-country limits.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: Employer files petition; only realistic if currently employed at a multinational with a US entity.

visa_routes.name: O-1A Extraordinary Ability

salary_threshold.note: 'High salary' is one of the evidentiary criteria, not a threshold.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: None; must show sustained national/international acclaim (meet at least 3 of the regulatory criteria, e.g. awards, publications, judging, critical role, high remuneration).
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Often paired with EB-1A or EB-2 NIW self-petition; India backlog still applies.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: US employer or agent petitions; legal fees significant. High evidentiary bar for a typical senior full-stack engineer.

sponsor_register.name: USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub (also: DOL OFLC LCA disclosure data)
sponsor_register.update_frequency: Not stated on page; data covers FY2009 through FY2026 Q4 as of 2026-11-22.
sponsor_register.how_to_use: Download annual files (Crosstab View → Download → CSV/Excel). Fields queryable by fiscal year, employer name, city, state, ZIP, NAICS; employers identified by name + last 4 of tax ID; counts are first-decision approvals/denials for initial and continuing employment. App: normalise employer names (lowercase, strip punctuation and suffixes like Inc/LLC/Corp/LP, '&'→'and'), aggregate across name variants, flag companies with recent 'initial approval' counts > 0 as likely H-1B sponsors. It is not a licence register: any US employer can file.

ease_for_indian_nationals.rationale: Highest pay, but the main route (H-1B) is an annual lottery (now wage-weighted, which favours senior offers), the employer must sponsor from abroad, a $100,000 new-petition fee is in force-but-blocked litigation that deters overseas hiring, a 3-year Indian degree needs an education+experience equivalency, and India-born green-card backlogs are very long.

factors.degree_recognition: 3-year degree not equivalent by itself; use 3-for-1 experience equivalency evaluation for H-1B.
factors.processing_speed: Fixed annual cycle: register March, start October at earliest.
factors.employer_willingness: Large H-1B ecosystem, but sponsoring candidates abroad is now costlier/riskier; many postings say 'no sponsorship'.
factors.attestation_or_paperwork: Credential evaluation, experience letters, LCA, petition, consular interview.

relocation_norms: Not researched from a citable source in this session; large tech firms commonly offer relocation for sponsored hires, but terms vary.

scam_warnings: Anyone selling a 'guaranteed H-1B' or charging the worker for lottery registration/sponsorship: the H-1B is lottery-based and employer-filed; no one can guarantee selection.

Body-shop/consultancy offers that file many registrations and 'bench' workers without pay or require bonds/penalty clauses; verify the employer in the H-1B Employer Data Hub and ask for the actual end client.
Recruiters asking for money for 'visa processing', training or interview slots; or offers made only over chat apps without interviews.
Claims that the $100,000 fee must be paid by the worker: the proclamation targets employers' petitions, and its status is in litigation.
